description.purpose: An interactive canvas of the colony, on a port of its own. A timer takes a topology snapshot, a code cell turns it into display objects, and a `web` cell holds them and serves the page. The browser owns the drag and the camera; nothing else.
description.use_when: Somebody should see and rearrange something the colony knows, in a browser. One canvy per canvas: two canvases are two hives on two ports, which is what makes one reverse-proxy rule a complete access statement for one of them.
description.not_in_scope: It draws nothing the topology snapshot does not hold, and that snapshot arrives on a timer through this hive's OWN lane to the colony's read-only graph endpoint (GH #163), so the canvas is as fresh as that timer. No authentication and no TLS: the display binds loopback by default and everything in front of it is somebody else's job (R-W8-2). No object library beyond cells, hives and edges. No interior address: `params.ports` is empty, so no cell in here is an endpoint -- a caller names the hive and a lane (in_refresh in, event out).
examples: GET http://127.0.0.1:7810/ -- the colony, draggable, arrangement persistent
a drag -> object:set on the node's x and y -> a diff to every open browser, without one message entering the colony
every minute: a topology snapshot -> one bundle of object calls -> the picture catches up
